prompt: Describe an integer by applying rules in priority order: "zero" first, then small vs large by absolute value, combined with even vs odd. Complete the describe method.
explanation: Condition order matters: 0 is even and |0| <= 10, so the zero check must run first or 0 would come back as "small even". Math.abs(n) lets one comparison cover both -10 and 10 for the size rule. For parity, n % 2 == 0 is the safe test on negatives -- in Java, -7 % 2 is -1 (not 1), so comparing against == 1 for odd would silently fail; testing for even (or != 0) sidesteps that trap.
hints: Return "zero" first -- if you test even/odd or size before the zero case, 0 will match the wrong rule.
Math.abs(n) <= 10 decides small vs large in one comparison for both positives and negatives.
For odd negatives, remember -7 % 2 is -1 in Java; test n % 2 == 0 for even and use else for odd.
